title: 5 Ways Hotels Can Rank on ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini
summary: 12 steps to get a hotel into ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode: AI crawlers, Business Profile, free booking links, OTA facts, reviews and agents.
body_markdown:
*Written by Punn Kam, ex-Google AI engineer and Y Combinator repeat founder. He is the co-founder of Conduit, an AI agent platform built for hospitality, serving 300+ hospitality brands in 140+ languages. Last updated October 8, 2026.*


A hotel shows up in ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews and other AI search by doing hotel SEO well and then a few things on top: letting AI search crawlers in, keeping Google Business Profile and rate feeds complete, keeping the same facts on every OTA, earning reviews and third-party mentions, and answering guest questions in plain text.


Each of the 12 steps below is marked "evidence-backed" when a vendor's own documentation or a credible study supports it, and "plausible" when only practitioner agreement or correlation does.


## How do hotels rank in ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews?


Hotels rank in ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews mostly through the same work as hotel SEO. Google says "there are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, nor other special optimizations necessary" beyond being indexed and eligible for a snippet ([Google Search Central](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) ). Cloudbeds' study of ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini answers across six destinations found that 55.3% of the sources cited for hotels were OTAs ([Hospitality Net, June 26, 2025](https://www.hospitalitynet.org/news/4127865.html) ), so your OTA pages are part of your AI presence.


Each engine also draws on its own pages: in our[study of 1,454 AI citations across 7 engines](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/ai-search-citation-study) , 76% of cited URLs appeared on one engine only. That data comes from 33 software-buyer prompts, not traveller prompts.


## Where can guests book hotels inside AI tools today?


Guests can book hotels inside Google AI Mode and search them inside ChatGPT, at small volume so far. Google began rolling out hotel booking in AI Mode in the US on August 27, 2026, with Booking.com, Choice, Expedia, Hilton, Hotels.com, IHG, Marriott, Priceline, Trip.com and Wyndham as partners; "the hotel or booking platform will act as the merchant of record" ([Google](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/book-travel-ai-mode/) ). The post does not say how independent hotels join.


In ChatGPT, Booking.com and Expedia launched travel apps in October 2025 ([Skift, October 6, 2025](https://skift.com/2025/10/06/expedia-booking-chatgpt-apps-openai/) ), and chains such as IHG have added their own ([Hotel Dive, June 4, 2026](https://www.hoteldive.com/news/ihg-hotels-resorts-launches-chatgpt-app/821979/) ). Booking Holdings said on August 4, 2026 that traffic from large language models was "still significantly below 1% of our room nights" ([transcript](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-booking-holdings-tops-q2-2026-forecasts-shares-jump-93CH-4836060) ).[Will AI agents replace Booking.com?](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/will-ai-agents-replace-booking-com) covers the OTA side.


## How do hotels let AI search engines read their website?


Hotels let AI search engines read their website by allowing the search crawlers in robots.txt and in the CDN or firewall, and by keeping key pages indexed in Google and Bing. OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity and Google each separate search access from training use, so a hotel can allow one and refuse the other.


### Step 1: Allow AI search crawlers (evidence-backed)


Allow OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot, Googlebot and Bingbot.


Crawler token Owner What the vendor says it does What blocking it does


OAI-SearchBot OpenAI Surfaces websites in ChatGPT's search features "Sites that are opted out of OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers"


GPTBot OpenAI Crawls content that "may be used in training" Opts out of training only


PerplexityBot Perplexity Surfaces and links sites in Perplexity results; "not used to crawl content for AI foundation models" Drops you from Perplexity results


Claude-SearchBot Anthropic "navigates the web to improve search result quality" "may reduce your site's visibility and accuracy in user search results"


ClaudeBot Anthropic Collects content that could contribute to model training Excludes future content from training


Google-Extended Google Controls use for Gemini training and grounding "does not impact a site's inclusion in Google Search", which includes AI Overviews and AI Mode


Sources, read October 8, 2026:[OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots) ,[Perplexity](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/bots) ,[Anthropic](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8896518-does-anthropic-crawl-data-from-the-web-and-how-can-site-owners-block-the-crawler) ,[Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/google-common-crawlers) .


### Step 2: Keep key pages indexed with snippets allowed (evidence-backed)


A page must be "indexed and eligible to be shown in Google Search with a snippet" to appear as a link in AI Overviews or AI Mode ([Google Search Central](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) ). For Copilot, check that Bing indexes the same pages.


## How do Google Business Profile and Hotel Center help a hotel show up in AI search?


Google Business Profile and Hotel Center help a hotel show up in AI search because Google's AI features read from the same systems as local search and hotel results. Google's AI-features page tells site owners to check that "Merchant Center and Business Profile information is up-to-date" ([Google Search Central](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) ).


### Step 3: Complete your Google Business Profile (evidence-backed for local search, plausible for AI)


Google's local ranking help says "businesses with complete and accurate info are more likely to show up in local search results" and that "more reviews and positive ratings can help your business's local ranking" ([Google Business Profile Help](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091?hl=en) ).


### Step 4: Turn on Google free booking links (evidence-backed for links, plausible for AI Mode)


Free booking links are "unpaid links, ranked according to their utility to users", and "hotel partners pay no fee" ([Google Hotel Center Help](https://support.google.com/hotelprices/answer/10472393?hl=en) ). Google stopped self-service rates in Business Profile on July 30, 2025 ([Hotel Center announcement](https://support.google.com/hotelprices/announcements/9652284) ), so you need a booking engine, CRS or PMS partner that connects to Google.


## Which hotel facts and pages do AI engines rely on?


AI engines rely on hotel facts that match across a hotel's website, Google, the OTAs and review sites, and on pages that answer a guest's question in readable text. When those sources disagree, an engine has no reason to prefer the hotel's own version.


### Step 5: Keep the same facts everywhere (plausible, with vendor data behind it)


Use the same name, address, room types, amenities, fees and policies on your site, Google Business Profile, every OTA and Tripadvisor. With OTAs at 55.3% of cited sources in Cloudbeds' study, your OTA listing copy is often the text an engine reads.


### Step 6: Build review volume and recency (evidence-backed for local, plausible for AI)


Ask every guest for a review on Google, Tripadvisor and the OTAs, and reply. Google says more reviews help local ranking; no study we found isolates their effect on AI answers.


### Step 7: Answer real guest questions in plain HTML (plausible)


Answer parking, check-in, pets, accessibility, distances and room differences as text on the page, not inside PDFs, images or a booking widget.


### Step 8: Keep structured data accurate (evidence-backed)


Use schema.org Hotel or LodgingBusiness markup. Google says "there's also no special schema.org structured data that you need to add" for AI features, and lists "making sure your structured data matches the visible text on the page" as a best practice.


## How do hotels get onto the pages ChatGPT and Google cite?


Hotels get onto the pages ChatGPT and Google cite by earning mentions on third-party lists, guides, forums and videos, because each engine draws on a different set. In our Brand Radar data from 33 software-buyer prompts (not traveller prompts), Google AI Overviews took 16% of its citations from YouTube, Reddit and social posts while ChatGPT took none, and Claude took 68% from listicles.


### Step 9: Earn mentions on lists, guides, Reddit and YouTube (evidence-backed, correlational)


Pitch destination "best hotels in X" guides, tourism boards and local press with specific facts, answer honestly on Reddit, and title videos with the question a guest would type. In Ahrefs' study of 75,000 brands, branded web mentions correlated with AI Overview visibility at 0.664, against 0.218 for backlinks ([Ahrefs, May 26, 2025](https://ahrefs.com/blog/ai-overview-brand-correlation/) ). Ahrefs sells AI-visibility tools and notes correlation is not causation.


## How can a hotel get ready for AI agents that book rooms?


A hotel gets ready for AI agents by making its rates reachable through a connected booking engine, and by answering the questions agents and guests ask before and after the booking on every channel. Independent hotels and short-term rental operators mostly reach agents through OTAs today, so their software vendors decide much of this step.


### Step 10: Ask your booking engine or PMS about agent access (evidence-backed that it exists, plausible on return)


Ask whether your booking engine, PMS or channel manager offers an MCP server or agent API. Apaleo launched an MCP server that lets AI agents check availability and modify bookings ([Apaleo, September 22, 2025](https://apaleo.com/blog/apaleo-news/apaleo-launches-mcp-server) ). For the booking side, see[How to Get Direct Bookings From ChatGPT and AI Agents](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/direct-bookings-from-chatgpt-ai-agents) .


### Step 11: Answer every guest question fast, before and after the booking (plausible)


Under AI Mode, the hotel or booking platform will "handle any customer service" ([Google](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/book-travel-ai-mode/) ). Answer phone, SMS, WhatsApp, email and OTA messages within minutes. Conduit's[AI agents](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) answer guest messages and calls at this step; Conduit does not take bookings or list rooms inside AI apps.


## How do you measure whether a hotel shows up in AI search?


You measure whether a hotel shows up in AI search with two free tools and a monthly manual check, since no single report covers every engine. Bing reports Copilot citations, Google folds AI Overviews into Search Console, and ChatGPT and Perplexity need a manual prompt panel.


### Step 12: Track citations and run a monthly prompt check (evidence-backed for the tools)


- Bing Webmaster Tools' AI Performance report shows how often Copilot and Bing's AI summaries cite your pages ([Bing Webmaster Blog](https://blogs.bing.com/webmaster/February-2026/Introducing-AI-Performance-in-Bing-Webmaster-Tools-Public-Preview) ).
- Google Search Console reports AI Overviews and AI Mode traffic "in the Performance report, within the 'Web' search type" ([Google Search Central](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) ).
- Once a month, ask ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Mode 10 to 20 real guest questions about your area and note who gets named and cited.


## What does the research on AI search for hotels not prove?


The research on AI search for hotels does not prove what causes a specific hotel to be recommended, because none of the studies cited on this page tests what changes a hotel's recommendations. Pew's independent study shows how few clicks an AI summary leaves. When one appeared, users clicked a traditional result in 8% of visits, against 15% without one ([Pew Research Center, July 22, 2025](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/) ).


## FAQ


Hotel owners often meet AI search through new terms such as GEO, llms.txt and AI crawlers, so the short answers below tie each term back to the 12 steps above. The vendor documentation behind them was read on October 8, 2026.


### How do I get my hotel to show up in ChatGPT?


To show up in ChatGPT, allow OAI-SearchBot, keep the same facts on your site and every OTA, earn reviews and mentions, and answer guest questions in plain text. OpenAI says sites that block OAI-SearchBot are not shown in ChatGPT search answers.


### Can you book a hotel in ChatGPT or Google AI Mode?


In Google AI Mode, US users can book with partners such as Booking.com, Expedia, Hilton and Marriott. In ChatGPT, Booking.com, Expedia and IHG apps search hotels in the chat.


### Should my hotel website have an llms.txt file?


An llms.txt file is optional and low priority for a hotel website. llms.txt is a proposal by Jeremy Howard, published September 3, 2024 ([llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org/) ). Google says you don't need "AI text files" for AI Overviews, and Google's John Mueller wrote in June 2025 that "no AI system currently uses llms.txt" ([Search Engine Roundtable](https://www.seroundtable.com/google-ai-llms-txt-39607.html) ).


### Should I block GPTBot or other AI crawlers on my hotel website?


A hotel should keep AI search bots open and block training bots only if it wants to. GPTBot, ClaudeBot and Google-Extended govern training and Gemini use; OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot and Claude-SearchBot decide whether you appear in those engines' answers.


### Is GEO different from hotel SEO?


GEO, generative engine optimization, is mostly the same work as hotel SEO: indexing, Business Profile, reviews and content, plus AI crawler access, consistent OTA content and mentions on the pages AI engines cite.
